sections.h2: Which way of selling suits an Eagan house?
sections.html:
Sellers in Eagan generally pick between hiring an agent, handling the sale themselves, or accepting a cash offer. Condition, schedule and tenants decide which one makes sense.

An agent listing draws the widest audience and works for a house in decent shape when you can allow showings. A cash purchase can suit a rental owner facing a new license cycle, an owner moving on a short timeline, or a house still carrying decades-old finishes. Ask each buyer for a written price and closing date, pull your permit history and any special assessment record, and compare the net amount each offer leaves you.

This Dakota County suburb sits south of Saint Paul and borders the Minnesota River on the west. Drivers rely on Interstate 35E and Minnesota Highways 13, 55, 77 and 149. Population stands at 67,109 in the 2025 estimate, roughly 2.5 percent under the 2020 base. Eagan grew fastest in the 1980s, doubling in a decade, which is why original roofs, windows and kitchens still turn up in resale listings.

sections.h2: Which school district is your Eagan address in?
sections.html:
Three districts serve Eagan addresses: Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan (District 196), West St. Paul-Mendota Heights-Eagan (District 197) and Burnsville-Eagan-Savage (District 191). Eagan High School, Blackhawk Middle School and Dakota Hills Middle School belong to District 196. Check the exact street before a listing names a school.

Eagan sits close to the Minneapolis-Saint Paul airport and the freeways, and warehouses and distribution centers cluster in the northern part of the city. A house near that area will draw a different buyer than one in a quiet residential pocket, so describe the setting honestly in your listing.

sections.h2: Does an Eagan rental license pass to the buyer?
sections.html:
No. The rental licensing ordinance dates from March 21, 2023. Each license covers one year and stays with the owner who applied, so a buyer must get a new one.

  • For 2026/27 a single-unit rental pays $165 a year plus a $25 application fee, and converting an owner-occupied home to a rental adds a $300 fee.
  • The city inspects each rental unit roughly every third year, or sooner after a complaint, and tenants must get at least 24 hours of notice.
  • Exemptions cover units rented to qualifying relatives of the owner, housing the state itself licenses, rooms within an owner-occupied home and contract-for-deed purchases recorded with Dakota County.

Renewing late adds 10 percent of the base fee in the first 30 days, 50 percent from 30 to 60 days and 100 percent after that. If tenants live in the house you are selling, call Community Development at 651-675-5681 first. Any buyer who keeps the tenants applies in their own name.

sections.h2: Permit and flood checks before a sale
sections.html:
The city issues permits on two tracks. Building permits are filed through the online ePermits system, and Building Inspections (651-675-5675) books 30-minute inspection slots on weekdays between 7:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. Projects that need no building permit get a zoning permit, which costs nothing.

Fences, patios, sport courts, driveway replacements, sidewalks, detached decks below 30 inches, one-story sheds up to 200 square feet, retaining walls under four feet and docks all fall under zoning permits. Staff generally reply within two to five business days. The city's property information page shows records and special assessments, and many files include scanned permits, inspection history and site surveys that let a buyer see what work was done.

On flood risk, every property is in FEMA Flood Zone X except those in Zone AE along the Minnesota River. The maps date from December 2, 2011, so call the Planning Department or FEMA to confirm an address.

sections.h2: Where an Eagan deed gets recorded
sections.html:
Only the Dakota County Administration Center in Hastings accepts deeds. You can book an appointment, or mail the deed to the Property Taxation and Records office, 1590 Highway 55, enclosing a cover letter, a stamped return envelope and your phone number.

Deed tax is 0.33 percent of the net price (Minnesota Statutes 287.21). A transfer deed must also include either a $54 well certificate or a signed well statement. Because most parcels here are abstract property, the title company searches the record before closing. Tax statements and valuation notices appear in the county's Property Information Search, and Property Taxation and Records takes questions at 651-438-4597.

Minnesota Statutes 513.55 also requires you to give the buyer a written list of known material facts before you sign.

sections.h2: Dakota County tax dates and payment
sections.html:
Property tax bills arrive in two halves, due May 15 and October 15. Paymentus handles online payments, charging 2.29 percent on cards, $2.95 on Visa debit or $0.35 for a bank transfer. Its phone line is 1-844-797-9075.

Counters at the Hastings, West St. Paul and Apple Valley buildings take payment on weekdays until 4:30 p.m. Mail must be postmarked by the due date. Owners without a mortgage company can sign up for free automatic payment.

A buyer who will live in the house should file the homestead application by December 31. Ask your closing agent how the year's tax gets prorated between you.

sections.h2: Getting an Eagan house ready for a buyer
sections.html:
Begin with documents: permit records and site surveys from the city's property page, plus the county tax statement. A tenant-occupied house also needs its rental license and newest inspection record. After that, choose how much work to do. Older finishes show better with fresh paint and serviced systems, though a cash buyer accepts the house untouched.

Get each offer in writing with a closing date. Then ask the title company for a payoff figure and for anything that might hold up recording. If a cash buyer is on the table, compare the final amount you would keep against a listing after repairs, showings and the wait for a lender, and pick the route that fits your calendar.

faqs.q: Will the buyer of my Eagan rental house inherit its license?
faqs.a: No transfer is possible. A license lasts one year, so the new owner applies for a fresh one. Community Development at 651-675-5681 can walk through the steps.

faqs.q: Which office takes a deed for recording in Dakota County?
faqs.a: The Property Taxation and Records office in Hastings. Book an appointment, or send the deed by mail to 1590 Highway 55 with a cover letter, return postage and a phone number.

faqs.q: Is my Eagan house in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Almost certainly not. Every property is in FEMA Flood Zone X except those in Zone AE along the Minnesota River. The maps date from 2011, so confirm an address with Planning or FEMA.

faqs.q: Does swapping out a fence or driveway before a sale need city approval in Eagan?
faqs.a: It needs a zoning permit, which is free. Fences, driveway replacements, patios, sheds up to 200 square feet and retaining walls under four feet are covered. Staff usually reply in two to five business days, and the Zoning Hotline is 651-675-5685.

faqs.q: When are Dakota County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half on May 15 and half on October 15. You can pay online, in person or by mail, and a mailed payment counts if it is postmarked by the due date.
